fieldValues.title: srs:// URIs have no query syntax, so a resource carries no knobs
fieldValues.summary: There is no place in an srs:// resource URI to put a depth parameter, so the tree resource serves TreeOptions::default() and a caller wanting a different depth has no way to ask. A per-member tree URI was likewise not added: instanceId already addresses tree/{instanceId}, and a URI is adapter vocabulary that does not belong on a service struct.
evidence: srs://<repoId>/tree serves tree_service::build_tree(TreeOptions::default()) with no way to vary depth
The descent hook is sectionContainerId — an id the client resolves — rather than a tree URI stamped onto ResolvedMember
uri.rs roundtrip and rejection tests define the accepted URI shapes; none of them admit a query string
fieldValues.body: Worth knowing before designing the next resource: anything parameterised has to become either a path segment or a tool, because the URI space is flat and unparameterised. The hook design follows from the same constraint and is the better shape anyway — handing the client an id it already knows how to address keeps adapter vocabulary out of the core's structs.
